title: IMD forecasts extremely heavy rainfall in Odisha and Gangetic West Bengal today - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Gangetic West Bengal and Odisha today following the formation of a low-pressure area over the North Bay of Bengal.

According to IMD, places over Chhattisgarh are expected to experience heavy to very heavy rainfall till tomorrow. Heavy rainfall is expected to prevail over Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Madhya Maharashtra and West Madhya Pradesh today.

Similar conditions will prevail over Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Konkan, Goa, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Vidarbha and the northeastern states for the day. Further, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Andaman and Nicobar Islands are expected to witness thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds during the next two days.

title: Shelter Collapse in India Leaves Missing After Heavy Rainfall - صوت الإمارات
article_text:
Itanagar, India — Authorities reported a devastating shelter collapse in India following flash floods and landslides triggered by heavy monsoon rains in the northeastern state of Arunachal Pradesh. Consequently, the cloudburst in the Dibang Valley swept away military shelters, leading to personnel going missing, according to details in India Today coverage. Furthermore, rescue teams managed to pull survivors from the debris as search operations continue across the region.

Rescue Operations Following Shelter Collapse in India





Joint search and rescue teams from the military and disaster response forces are navigating treacherous weather and difficult terrain to locate missing individuals. Additionally, coverage by NDTV Profit reporting notes that a separate landslide at a road construction site caused casualties among infrastructure workers in the state.

Regional Damage and Infrastructure Disruptions





On the other hand, torrential rains have damaged hundreds of roads, bridges, and water facilities throughout the mountainous region. Consequently, meteorological authorities urged residents and travellers to exercise caution and avoid landslide-prone routes.





Finally, emergency agencies remain deployed to clear blocked highways and restore essential connectivity. Ultimately, mitigating seasonal flood risks requires sustained infrastructure reinforcement across vulnerable hill districts.

title: IMD Issues Orange Alert for Heavy Rain in Northeast - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department has issued an orange alert for heavy rainfall in the North-eastern region tomorrow. The IMD said that Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Chandigarh, Haryana, Delhi, Uttarakhand, Bihar, and Jharkhand are also expected to experience thundersquall conditions tomorrow.

The Met Department also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Interior Karnataka, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Kerala, Mahe, Madhya Pradesh, and Vidarbha for the next two days. Similar conditions are likely to prevail over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Coastal Karnataka, Rayalaseema, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal for the next two to three days.

The weather agency also forecast hot and humid conditions over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal for the next two to three days.

title: Weather Update: Delhi, UP On Heavy Rain Alert As Arunachal Floods Worsen, 5 Army Personnel Missing - The Daily Jagran
article_text:
By Nidhi Giri
Sun, 16 Aug 2026 07:49 AM (IST)
Source:JND
Add as a preferred
RELATED ARTICLES
HIGHLIGHTS
IMD warns of heavy rain, thunderstorms across India.
Five Army personnel missing in Arunachal Pradesh floods.
Landslides claim four lives in Arunachal Pradesh.

Weather Update: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a warning of heavy to very heavy rain, thunderstorms, and strong winds in many parts of India on Sunday. Bad weather is expected in Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, as well as the northeastern states. The flood and landslide situation in Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Sikkim has worsened due to the heavy rains already continuing in the state.

Five Army personnel went missing after flash floods swept away two shelters at an Army camp in Arunachal Pradesh's Dibang Valley district, while four people were killed in a landslide at a road construction site in Upper Subansiri district.

ALSO READ: Uttarakhand Weather: Heavy Rain Batters Dehradun, Pithoragarh, Bageshwar; 105 Roads Closed

Delhi-NCR and North India

Heavy rain and thunderstorms are expected at isolated places in Delhi-NCR. Strong winds with speeds of 40 to 50 kilometre per hour are possible during this period. The maximum temperature is expected to be 34 degrees Celsius and the minimum temperature is expected to be 28 degrees Celsius

UP Weather

Several districts in Uttar Pradesh are on alert for heavy rain and thunderstorms. These include Meerut, Muzaffarnagar, Gautam Buddha Nagar, Aligarh, Mathura, Agra, Kanpur, Bijnor, Saharanpur, Shamli, Badaun, Shahjahanpur, Etawah, Lakhimpur Kheri, Auraiya, Jalaun, Hamirpur, Firozabad, Ayodhya, Basti, Bulandshahr, Ghazipur, Gorakhpur, Prayagraj, and Deoria. Wind speeds could reach 60-70 kmph in some areas.

ALSO READ: Bihar Weather: Rain To Lash Several Areas, Thunderstorms Likely On August 16 | Check Forecast

Bihar Weather

Heavy rain and storm alert has been issued in West Champaran, Siwan, Gopalganj, Saran, East Champaran, Patna, Gaya, Bhojpur, Buxar, Vaishali, Samastipur, Darbhanga, Madhubani, Purnia, Kishanganj, Araria, Katihar, Bhagalpur, Khagaria and Begusarai districts of Bihar.

Rain Alert In Hilly States

Widespread rainfall is expected in Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir. The risk of landslides remains in mountainous areas. The Meteorological Department has advised avoiding unnecessary travel in these areas.

Floods Wreak Havoc In Northeast

Heavy to very heavy rainfall continues in Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Sikkim. Flooding and landslides have worsened the situation in several districts of Arunachal Pradesh, disrupting road traffic in some areas, disrupting normal life. Rising river levels in Assam have also affected several areas. Landslides have been reported in Sikkim, prompting local authorities to increase their vigilance.

According to the Meteorological Department, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam-Meghalaya, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim.
